customManagers.description: gitleaks: the GITLEAKS_VERSION env and installer default (written without a v) and the pre-commit rev (written with one). The value is captured without the v and releases are read without it, so each site keeps its own form. hack/test/consistency_toolchain_pins_test.sh (DTP-4) checks every site is extracted.

ShellCheck: the SHELLCHECK_VERSION env and installer default. Its bump PR stays red until hack/install-shellcheck.sh's pinned_sha256 table has the new digests (the intended manual step), so the shellcheck rule below keeps it out of every other group.

ShellCheck for pre-commit: the shellcheck-py rev (four components; the fourth is the wrapper's packaging revision). Tracked as its own tag so the bot writes a rev that exists; grouped with koalaman/shellcheck by the shellcheck rule below.

git-cliff outside Taskfile.yml: the orhun/git-cliff-action version input (the github-actions manager bumps the action, not the binary it installs) and the install-git-cliff.sh call in verify-changelog.sh. Same depName as the Taskfile pin, so all three land in one group.
golangci-lint: Makefile GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION and the custom build's version in hack/tooling/.custom-gcl.yml, one depName so they move together.
Helm release versions in CI and install scripts

go-task versions in the CI actions AND the mise.toml pin that mirrors them. Both resolve to depName go-task/task and both are custom.regex, so the 'pinned build tools' rule below lands them in ONE pull request instead of letting mise.toml go stale behind a workflow bump -- the same reasoning as the helm/helm rule. hack/test/consistency_toolchain_pins_test.sh is the fail-closed backstop if this ever stops matching.

packageRules.description: Bump the go directive of go.mod. The gomod manager never proposes it by default (docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/gomod); without this rule the golang image moves alone and the shipped binary is built by a Go the tests never ran. Scoped to the root go.mod so test fixtures keep their own directive.

Keep every Helm pin on one version. The azure/setup-helm input in release.yaml is seen by the github-actions manager while the annotated HELM_VERSION pins are seen by the custom manager, so without this they land in different groups and drift apart -- which is exactly how release.yaml reached v3.21.4 while CI stayed on v3.17.3. Both resolve to depName helm/helm.

ShellCheck in a group of its own: its bump PR is red until hack/install-shellcheck.sh gets the new digests, and must hold back no other tool. After 'pinned build tools' (a later groupName wins), before 'go toolchain' (which stays last).

golangci-lint in a group of its own: a new release often adds findings or breaks on a Go bump (CFC-2 builds and runs it), and its red PR must hold back no other tool. After 'pinned build tools', before 'go toolchain'.

Hold cel-go below 0.32. v0.32.0 renamed its module path to cel.dev/cel-go, and k8s.io/apiserver still imports github.com/google/cel-go, so taking it is a module migration, not a bump. Revisit together with the k8s.io modules once a k8s.io release imports cel.dev/cel-go.

Move the go directive and every golang image (Dockerfiles, devcontainer) in ONE pull request. Must stay the LAST rule that sets a groupName: a later rule's groupName wins, and any later group rule could pull go or golang out of this one. hack/test/consistency_go_toolchain_test.sh checks presence and position.

Keep the node-version and python-version inputs of actions/setup-node and actions/setup-python out of the bot. The github-actions manager extracts them (depType uses-with, depNames node and python), so a bump would land in the 'github actions' group without mise.toml, and hack/test/consistency_toolchain_pins_test.sh (DEV-MISE-01) would red that whole group PR. They are bumped by hand together with mise.toml, and the guard checks they agree. Last rule, so no later rule can re-enable them; it sets no groupName, so 'go toolchain' stays the last group rule.
